Templates: tenancy agreement, welcome emails, bank details

Upload your agreement as it is. Its blanks are filled in: PROPERTY ADDRESS, TENANCY START DATE, LANDLORD NAME, [LEAD TENANT], [TENANT 2]…, [GUARANTOR 1]…, [£RENT], [DEPOSIT], [FIRST RENT DATE], [RENT DAY], [SECOND RENT], [Deposit Scheme] and the "agreement made on" date. Signature boxes follow the number of tenants and guarantors.

These appear as quick-add buttons on each tenancy. Leave the amount empty to type it in each time. Press Save templates to keep changes.

Goes in the tenants’ welcome email when the tenancy has a DIY check-in, so they can use the DIY check-in without paying. Change it here whenever you change it on the DIY app.

🏛 Council tax links by borough

The welcome email works out the property’s borough from its postcode and links to that council’s council tax registration. Each link is checked before it’s used; type your own to replace any.

📜 Property licensing schemes by borough

All = the whole borough · Parts = certain wards or streets · None = no scheme · Not sure = changing or unclear. Used for the licence check on the landlord page. Councils change their schemes every few years — correct any that are out of date and add the council’s licensing page.

Formatting: [b]bold[/b], [u]underline[/u], [red]red and bold[/red], [small]small print[/small]. [clerk]…[/clerk] only when an inventory clerk is booked; [diy]…[/diy] only for a DIY check-in.

Filled in automatically: {{address}}, {{payment_reference}}, {{council_tax}} (the borough's council tax registration, worked out from the postcode), {{landlord_name}}, {{tenant_names}}, {{start_date}}, {{move_in_due}}, {{standing_order_start}}, {{standing_order_payments}}, {{first_rent}}, {{deposit}}, {{move_in_total}}, {{holding_deposit}}, {{move_in_remaining}}, {{checkin_date}}, {{checkin_time}}, {{diy_link}}, {{diy_code}} (the DIY check-in access code, added after the DIY link automatically), {{payment_link}} (the tenants’ link to upload proof of payment — a button is added after the bank details automatically), {{bank_details}}, {{signature}}, {{year}}.

🗓 Pre-viewing reservations (PVR)

Send a PVR from “Send a form to an applicant” above. They sign and pay one week’s rent to reserve before viewing, then tell us within 24 hours if they’re going ahead — yes takes them to the offer form (the PVR becomes their holding deposit), no asks for their account for the refund.

👥 Staff access to offers

Give staff this link and the staff password. They can only see and work on offers — accept or reject, mark deposits, right to rent checks, tracking links and the PDF. They can’t delete offers or see anything else in Fixflow. Everything they do is noted on the offer.

🔔 Phone alerts for staff

Staff get an alert when an offer comes in, is accepted or rejected, a holding deposit arrives, or an applicant says they’ve paid. They install the free ntfy app and subscribe to this channel (or open the link on their phone):

📎 Upload a gas safety, EICR, EPC or property licenceFixflow reads which property it’s for and the dates — check them and save. Or drag & drop it here.

🌐 Website bookings — gas safety, EICR, EPC & tenants’ cleaning prices

Landlords can book and pay for these at residentialrealtors.co.uk/book-certificate. The end-of-tenancy clean, oven and carpet services are for tenants moving out, at residentialrealtors.co.uk/book-a-clean — give them a price to switch them on (left blank, they aren’t offered). Enter prices excluding VAT — the website adds VAT at 20%. Type 0 for a free service; leave it empty to hide it. Each booking appears in Website leads and raises a job for the contractor you choose for that service.

Welcome email

info@residentialrealtors.co.uk is always copied in.

First time: make it open straight in Outlook (Classic)
  1. Press Open in Outlook once. The email downloads (a file ending .eml).
  2. In Windows, right-click the downloaded file → Open with → Choose another app → pick Outlook (classic) → Always.
  3. In Edge or Chrome, click the ⋯ next to the download → Always open files of this type.

After that, each time you press Open in Outlook, a new Outlook message pops up with the formatting and documents already in it — just press Send.

Let the tenant know

New invoice to the landlord

Lists labour, each material and the small extras (silicone, fixings…). With a total it splits it exactly; without one it suggests typical London prices — check them before sending.

The landlord sees the lines, notes and total — don’t include contractor names or what we pay.

Anniversary fees to charge

These tenancies pay the fee up front and are in month 12. Charge the landlord the fee for the next year (on the rent for that year) — “Charged” creates the invoice for the landlord.

Landlord statements to send

A statement for each rent date. Where the landlord owed us from an earlier statement (e.g. the move-in fees were more than the first rent), it is brought forward and taken from this month’s rent — the ones still owing are at the top.

Recover from the rent

Rent is due on these tenancies and the landlord has unpaid invoices. Take the amount from the rent you pass on, then mark it recovered (the invoices are marked paid).
